statusText: CME equity futures are halted for ten of the twenty-four published hours and no U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside the window, holding Tail at the closed-venue floor. Every Friday primary mark re-verified unchanged this run. Two verified additions frame the week: the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance takes effect Monday with SpaceX confirmed at 2.82%, and Hormuz throughput is reported at a six-month high as the physical supply panic continues to ease.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. headline: A confirmed Nasdaq-100 rebalance for Monday and a Hormuz corridor reported at six-month throughput join an otherwise unchanged weekend ledger: the venue stays halted for ten of the 24 published hours and two-way discovery still frames the 22:00Z restart
body:
Ten of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt; the remaining fourteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session that follows and the European hours into Monday morning. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day. Every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources for this run and all are unchanged: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08% from 15.44, inside a 14.80-15.63 day range and near the lower end of its 13.38-35.30 annual range. WTI settled 100.30 and Brent 103.87, a third consecutive easier session, although WTI remains up about 18.85% over the month. Federal Reserve H.15 for 17 September shows the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%.

Two verified items are new to this run. The first is index-structural: the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance takes effect on Monday 21 September, and SpaceX's weight is confirmed at 2.82%, up from about 1.28%, calculated on Friday's close. More than 200 funds tracking over 800 billion dollars follow the index, so the change carries a known passive-flow checkpoint into Monday's U.S. session, which falls after the last hour published here. The second is geopolitical and permissive: crude and LNG throughput through the Strait of Hormuz is reported at a six-month high under naval escort, with roughly 10 million barrels a day moving through the waterway and the supply situation described as stabilising. That sits against an unresolved Red Sea leg, where transits through Bab el-Mandeb are reported down from about 29-30 daily to 12 after the Perim Island seizure, and against the 16 September FOMC decision to raise the target range 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00%, the first increase since 2023, with a dot plot pointing to one more move this year. Separately, China left its 1-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and its 5-year at 3.50% on Sunday for a sixteenth month, matching every forecast in a 21-participant poll.

That balance is why the published scores separate the way they do. Stress eases one point to 30 in the moderate band: the oil-led inflation channel is marginally less acute with Hormuz throughput improving, while a hiking Fed, long-end yields near 4.94%, a crowded crude book and a catalyst-dense week remain in place. Tail holds at 5 because Tail measures a pathological price path that denies retracement, and a halted venue cannot exhibit one; a VIX of 14.81 and a Friday close near the day's high are not evidence of that path either. Dominant mode is normal because no venue is open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence of 76 reflects fully re-verified levels, yields, crude and volatility, a verified seven-day calendar and two newly corroborated catalysts; the single gap, live price-path evidence, is structural to the weekend halt rather than a defect in the research. The shared cross-asset context file was stale and partial for this run, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so this assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first ten slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final seven slots. Stress opened at 22, drifted through 23 and 24 across Saturday afternoon and evening, stepped to 26 after midnight, eased to 25, then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation reporting landed and climbed to 30 and finally 31 through the Sunday morning hours. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence began at 76, troughed at 72 at 21:00Z Saturday as distance from the Friday tape grew, and recovered into the mid-70s as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Ten of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the remaining fourteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session and the European hours into Monday morning. Cash closed Friday 18 September and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday, 18:00 ET. No U.S. macro release falls anywhere inside this window; the only scheduled U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday, and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour, then steps through 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13 across the European Sunday afternoon and evening before reaching 15 in the last pre-restart hour. It tops the window at 18 at the 22:00Z restart, eases to 17 for the first full hour, then decays through 15, 14, 13, 12, 11 and 10 across the Asian session before ticking to 11 at the European cash open and 12 for the Goolsbee checkpoint and the final hour, where the Monday index rebalance adds a known flow consideration. That drift tracks time-to-restart and session transitions rather than observed structure, and every published hour stays inside the EA_ON band. Stress holds between 30 and 34, peaking at the restart. Confidence troughs at 71 immediately before and at the restart, then rises to 78 as a live tape re-accumulates.
